title: Bind Claude telemetry to the durable launcher
description: Prerequisite for task-00e4827dd9374ec79625351d560c82c8. Fresh measurement at HEAD 8557296: launchClaudeWithTelemetry hardwires raw launchClaude and returns only the telemetry handoff, while Foundation dispatch must use createClaudeLauncher(authority) and still needs the exact ClaudeLaunchResult. Add the public runner factory/result surface that executes one authority-bound physical launch and derives the handoff from that same result—never a second launch or a rebuilt observation.
definitionOfDone: A public @moe/runner factory accepts only ClaudeLauncherAuthority, binds createClaudeLauncher(authority), and on invocation calls that launcher exactly once; no caller-supplied deps, launcher function, exit, observation, or telemetry handoff is accepted.

The success arm returns one deeply frozen object containing the exact ClaudeLaunchResult and the ClaudeTelemetryHandoff derived from that same result; REFUSED, EXIT_BEFORE_LAUNCH, ADOPTED and OBSERVED preserve the runner's existing truth, code and layer without restamping.

A malformed/hostile ProviderRunRef refuses at TELEMETRY_INPUT with TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED before authority, store, filesystem, or process effects; generated hostile cases assert a positive case count.

Focused production-surface tests prove one-launch ordering, raw-result identity/binding, blind UNKNOWN behavior, and one accepted same-result control; mutation of the production binding to invoke twice or pair a different result reddens a named assertion.

The new symbol is exported through the public @moe/runner root, the existing daemon manifest and pnpm-lock edge remain valid, and a compiled bare-specifier probe from apps/daemon typechecks and is deleted in the same command.
taskRails: Modify only packages/runner/src/providers/telemetry/claude-telemetry-launch.ts, its focused test, and packages/runner/src/surface/claude-surface.ts; refactor/trim the existing 250-line production source rather than growing it over 250.
Do not expose private launcher defaults, snapshotRunRef, intakeProcessObservation, raw dependencies, or a generic supplied-launcher hook; authority is the existing public ClaudeLauncherAuthority.
Preserve existing ProviderTelemetryCode/layer and Claude launcher refusals exactly; no new wire kind or daemon behavior in this task.
Use TDD, assert exact code/layer and nonzero cases, run runner typecheck/test with nonzero count lines, and name task-00e4827dd9374ec79625351d560c82c8 as the consuming production task.

implementationPlan.description:
REFACTOR FIRST, BEHAVIOUR UNCHANGED. In claude-telemetry-launch.ts, extract the arm-selection body of `launchClaudeWithTelemetry` into one internal `handoffOf(providerRunRef, declared, result): ClaudeTelemetryHandoff` that takes an ALREADY-OBTAINED `ClaudeLaunchResult` and performs no launching. It keeps the three existing arms exactly as they are today: REFUSED -> `blindHandoff(..., "TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED", "REFUSED", "LAUNCH_REFUSED")`; any non-OBSERVED kind (ADOPTED, EXIT_BEFORE_LAUNCH) -> `blindHandoff(..., "TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED", "UNKNOWN", "LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED")`; OBSERVED -> the parsed handoff. Do not renumber codes, do not reorder the arms, do not touch `blindHandoff`, `factsOf`, `infrastructureOf`, `concurrencyOf`, `declaredOf` or `receipt`.
`launchClaudeWithTelemetry` then becomes: snapshot the run ref, refuse `TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED` / `TELEMETRY_INPUT`, read `declared`, `await launchClaude(...)`, return `{ok: true, handoff: handoffOf(...)}`.
THE PROOF THIS REFACTOR IS BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING is the existing 526-line suite: it must stay green WITHOUT edits to its existing cases. If an existing assertion has to change, the refactor changed behaviour — stop and re-derive rather than editing the test to match.
Measure `wc -l` after this step and record it; the extraction should be roughly line-neutral, and the number is the budget the factory must fit inside.

implementationPlan.description:
ADD THE FACTORY, and keep the file at or under 250 physical lines.
- `export interface ClaudeBoundLaunch { readonly ok: true; readonly result: ClaudeLaunchResult; readonly handoff: ClaudeTelemetryHandoff }` and `export type ClaudeBoundLaunchResult = ClaudeBoundLaunch | ProviderTelemetryRefusal`.
- `export function createTelemetryBoundClaudeLauncher(authority: ClaudeLauncherAuthority): (input: ClaudeTelemetryLaunchInput) => Promise<ClaudeBoundLaunchResult>`. The parameter is TYPED as `ClaudeLauncherAuthority` even though `createClaudeLauncher` takes `unknown` — that type is the compile-time fence the DoD asks for; the launcher still decodes at runtime.
- Bind `const launch = createClaudeLauncher(authority)` ONCE, at factory time, and close over it. On invocation: snapshot the run ref FIRST and refuse `TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED` / `TELEMETRY_INPUT` before anything else; read `declared`; `const result = await launch(input.request, input.options ?? {})` — exactly one call, on one line, with no retry, no fallback to `launchClaude`, and no second invocation on any arm; return `deepFreeze({ ok: true, result, handoff: handoffOf(providerRunRef, declared, result) })` passing THAT SAME `result` binding to `handoffOf`.
- No caller-supplied deps, launcher function, exit, observation or handoff is accepted anywhere in the signature; `ClaudeTelemetryLaunchInput` already carries only providerRunRef/request/options.
- Do NOT export `handoffOf`, `snapshotRunRef`, `intakeProcessObservation`, `CLAUDE_LAUNCHER_DEFAULTS` or any private default (rail 2).
TRIMMING TO FIT: compress multi-line type and constant declarations in this file toward the density the surrounding package already uses. Do NOT delete the two load-bearing notes in the header — that `declared` and `observedModel` are never merged, and that `declaredCeiling` and `achieved` never become one another. If the file still exceeds 250 after honest compression, report blocked with the measured count rather than deleting those notes or silently exceeding the rail.

THE FOUR ARMS, each asserting the exact truth class, code and layer, and each asserting the raw result travels with the handoff.
- REFUSED: the launcher's own `code` and `layer` appear verbatim as `handoff.launch.reasonCode` / `reasonLayer`; `handoff.telemetryRefusal` carries `TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED` at `TELEMETRY_LAUNCH`; terminal is `REFUSED`, infrastructure `LAUNCH_REFUSED`; and `bound.result.kind === "REFUSED"` is still returned rather than swallowed.
- EXIT_BEFORE_LAUNCH and ADOPTED, as two SEPARATE cases: both take the not-attempted arm with `TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED`, terminal `UNKNOWN`, infrastructure `LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED` — but assert each kind independently, because a single case would stay green if one kind stopped reaching that arm.
- OBSERVED: `truthClass`, digests, timestamps and `exit` all come from `result.observation`, and `infrastructure` is `NONE` only when the exit was observed, the capture parsed AND the launcher proved the run.
- BLIND UNKNOWN BEHAVIOUR: on every non-OBSERVED arm the token, step, model, sequence and receipt facts are UNKNOWN carrying the forwarded code and layer — never zero-filled, never partially summed. Assert the UNKNOWN's code, not merely that the value is not a number.
No restamping: a launcher refusal must never be reported under a TELEMETRY_* code, and a telemetry refusal must never be reported under a launcher code.

HOSTILE ProviderRunRef, refused before any effect — DoD item 3.
Generate the hostile cases: null, undefined, a primitive, an array, a Proxy with a throwing `get`, a revoked Proxy, an object with an accessor-backed field, `__proto__`-bearing, missing one required ref field, an empty-string field, a non-NFC field, and a numeric field where a string is required. Assert `cases.length > 0` BEFORE asserting outcomes — a sweep that silently generates zero cases passes while testing nothing.
Every case must return the refusal `{ code: "TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED", layer: "TELEMETRY_INPUT" }` — assert BOTH, never just `ok === false`.
AND ASSERT ZERO EFFECTS, which is the half a return-value assertion cannot see: drive each case through a factory built over a BOOBY-TRAPPED authority whose `consumeGrantDurably` and `commitProcessRegistration` both throw if called, and assert neither was invoked. A hostile ref that reached the launcher would surface as that throw. Pair it with a positive control on the same authority shape — a well-formed ref DOES reach `consumeGrantDurably` — so the zero-effect assertion cannot be passing because the ports are unreachable in this fixture at all.

PUBLISH THE SYMBOL, and repair the closed roster it breaks.
In packages/runner/src/surface/claude-surface.ts, add `createTelemetryBoundClaudeLauncher`, `type ClaudeBoundLaunch` and `type ClaudeBoundLaunchResult` to the existing export block from `../providers/telemetry/claude-telemetry-launch.js`, and extend that block's doc comment with one sentence saying what the new entry point adds over `launchClaudeWithTelemetry`: it takes the durable authority instead of the shipped defaults and returns the raw `ClaudeLaunchResult` alongside the handoff, from ONE launch. Keep withholding `handoffOf` and every fact-minting helper. `packages/runner/src/index.ts:162` already re-exports this module, so the root gains the symbol with no index edit.
FORCED FOURTH FILE, and record it as such: packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts holds a closed root roster — `EXPECTED_EXPORTS.length` is asserted `toBe(232)` at :374 and the next case compares `Object.keys(runner).sort()` against the hand-written list with "no loss and no addition". A new root export reddens both, so satisfying DoD item 5 is impossible without editing it. Task rail 1 lists three files; this is a deliberate, forced deviation, not scope creep — state it in the completion notes with the two line numbers as evidence.
The edit is exactly three things: add `["createTelemetryBoundClaudeLauncher", "function"]` to the telemetry group of EXPECTED_EXPORTS; change 232 to 233; and update that group's hand-counted comment from "The 17 values ... and the 2 entry points" to 18 values and 3 entry points, since the comment says it is counted by hand from claude-surface.ts. Do NOT weaken the roster to a subset or `>=` check — its entire value is that a new root export cannot land unnoticed.

CONSUMER-EDGE PROBE from the consuming package — DoD item 5. The daemon manifest and lock edge already exist (step 1(f)); this proves the NEW symbol is reachable across it.
Write apps/daemon/src/_runner-bound-launch-probe.ts containing exactly an import of `createTelemetryBoundClaudeLauncher` and `type ClaudeBoundLaunchResult` from the BARE specifier `@moe/runner` plus one exported reference to both, run `npx tsc --project apps/daemon/tsconfig.json --noEmit`, require EXIT=0, and DELETE the probe in the SAME command so it cannot reach a commit. A root-barrel grep does not satisfy this rail, and neither does a relative import — this repo has no tsconfig paths and no project references, so a deep relative import fails TS6059 and would prove the opposite of what is claimed.
Record the command and its exit code verbatim. Note in the completion notes that this task adds NO daemon behaviour (task rail 3); the probe is evidence of reachability only, and apps/daemon is not an owned path of this task — nothing under it may remain modified.

MUTATION DRILLS — DoD item 4 names two of these explicitly, and a green suite cannot show any of them. Run each, record the exact test name that reddened, restore, and confirm the restored bytes hash-match the original (git status alone is unreliable in this shared worktree).

The raw-result identity assertion must redden — this is the drill that proves the handoff and the returned result come from the SAME launch rather than merely agreeing by luck.
3. DROP THE REF CHECK: delete the `providerRunRef === null` refusal from the factory. The hostile sweep must redden AND the booby-trapped authority must throw, proving the guard is what stops the effect rather than something downstream.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) ADD A NEW MODULE for the bound launcher (e.g. claude-bound-launch.ts). REJECTED by task rail 1, which names the three files that may change. It also would not help: the factory must share the arm-selection body with `launchClaudeWithTelemetry`, and splitting them across modules would either export the shared helper (rail 2 forbids publishing internals) or duplicate the arm logic, which is the disagreeing-second-derivation the module's own header warns about.
2) GIVE THE FACTORY A SUPPLIED-LAUNCHER HOOK so tests can count invocations directly. REJECTED by rail 2 and by the DoD: no caller-supplied launcher function. The honest observation point is the AUTHORITY — `consumeGrantDurably` is invoked by the real launcher during a real launch — so the one-launch property is asserted by counting authority-port calls, which is a production surface rather than a test seam.
3) CALL `createClaudeLauncher(authority)` PER INVOCATION instead of at factory time. REJECTED: the DoD says the factory BINDS the launcher, and rebinding per call would re-run composition on every launch while making "exactly one launch" harder to reason about. Bound once, closed over.
4) RETURN THE RAW RESULT ONLY ON THE OBSERVED ARM. REJECTED: the consumer needs exit facts precisely on the arms where the handoff is blind. Every arm returns the raw `ClaudeLaunchResult`; only the handoff goes UNKNOWN.
5) LEAVE THE ROOT ROSTER ALONE and publish only from claude-surface.ts. REJECTED as impossible: packages/runner/src/index.ts:162 re-exports claude-surface wholesale, so the symbol lands on the root either way and the roster at index-surface.test.ts:374 goes red. See the forced-deviation note below.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD d2151d49 (the description's 8557296 is stale; every structural claim it makes still holds).

THE FILE IS EXACTLY 250 LINES. `packages/runner/src/providers/telemetry/claude-telemetry-launch.ts` = 250, and task rail 1 forbids growing it past 250 and forbids adding a module. So the factory only fits after extracting the arm-selection body into an internal `handoffOf(providerRunRef, declared, result)` and compressing declarations. That extraction is also what makes the two entry points share ONE derivation instead of two that could disagree.

WHAT `launchClaudeWithTelemetry` DOES TODAY: snapshots the run ref and refuses TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED / TELEMETRY_INPUT BEFORE launching, reads `declared` through the launcher's own `snapshotLaunchSelection`, calls the hardwired `launchClaude(request, options ?? {})`, then branches REFUSED -> blind handoff (TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED / REFUSED / LAUNCH_REFUSED), non-OBSERVED -> blind handoff (TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED / UNKNOWN / LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED), OBSERVED -> parsed handoff. It returns ONLY `{ok, handoff}` — the `ClaudeLaunchResult` is discarded, which is the gap this task closes.
